chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The pilgrims return in three types: a type who is emancipated from the Fire, and a type who is freed from his sins as if he were like the day his mother gave him birth, and a type who is preserved regarding his family and his wealth. So that is the lowest of what the pilgrim returns with.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three levels of reward for pilgrims returning from Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines a hierarchy of spiritual outcomes for pilgrims, ranging from the ultimate deliverance from Hellfire to the preservation of one's worldly assets, which serves as the baseline reward. This classification reflects the Shia understanding of Hajj as a transformative act where the degree of sincerity and ritual perfection determines whether one achieves total sin remission or merely divine protection. The emphasis on 'preservation of family and wealth' highlights the holistic nature of the pilgrimage, ensuring that even those with lesser spiritual attainment receive tangible divine favor.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Pilgrims are arriving back being upon three types – a type who is emancipated (liberated) from the Fire, and a type who is exited from his sins as if he was like the day his mother gave him birth, and a type who received Protection regarding his family and his wealth. So that is the lowest of what the Pilgrim returns with’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Pilgrims (al-Hujjaj) are of three categories. Those in one group are set free from hellfire, the other group are made free of sins like their freedom from sin on the day their mother gave birth to them, and the third group consists of those who receive protection for their families and properties and this is the minimum benefit with which pilgrims return home.”’
